correctness.rationale: The Petersen graph is explicitly KG(5,2); its ordinary matching complex is exhaustively enumerated with 332 simplices including the empty simplex, and exact rational boundary ranks (1,14,61,79,6) give reduced Betti ranks five in degrees 2 and 3 only. For every S5 conjugacy type, signed-orbit invariant chain matrices are constructed from complete oriented boundaries and eliminated exactly over Q. The invariant homology dimension table and cyclic averaging recover H2/H3 characters, which equal the sign-twisted five-point permutation module and Specht (3,2). An independent direct modular chain-action computation reproduces all seven pairs, but is not used as sole proof. Fully standalone Python standard-library code and the complete table appear in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph has a canonical full S5 automorphism action, and its ordinary matching complex already has a natural mixed-dimensional homology with equal Betti numbers five in two degrees. Those equal ranks do not reveal the surprising contrast: a reducible sign-twisted permutation representation in degree 2 and the irreducible Specht (3,2) module in degree 3. This is a complete, natural equivariant invariant and a useful test case for graph complex topology, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of known ranks. No paper-sized consequence or claim of integral module classification is presumed.
